experiment_description: Bulk cadmium phosphorus trisulfide (CdPS3) single crystals from 2D Semiconductors Inc. were mechanically exfoliated under ambient conditions using Nitto Denko adhesive tape. For structural and compositional characterization, exfoliated CdPS3 flakes were transferred onto porous SiNx TEM grids by a dry-transfer process assisted by a PDMS support layer, and additional bulk flakes were transferred onto Si substrates. High-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy was performed using a Titan Themis Z transmission/scanning electron microscope equipped with spherical-aberration correction, in high-angle annular dark-field imaging mode, to inspect the crystal lattice of the exfoliated material. Chemical composition was measured by energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy using a Bruker QUANTAX EDX spectrometer integrated into a JEOL JSM-7001F scanning electron microscope operated in secondary-electron imaging mode; elemental maps were collected for Cd, P, and S over the exfoliated flake area.

measured_stoichiometric_formula.description: Chemical formula inferred from EDX elemental analysis of exfoliated CdPS3 flakes, based on the measured Cd, P, and S atomic proportions.

cd_p_s_atomic_ratio.description: Measured Cd:P:S stoichiometric ratio inferred from EDX, reported as matching the nominal crystal stoichiometry.

experiment_description: Angle-resolved Raman spectroscopy was performed on bulk CdPS3 flakes at ambient conditions using a Horiba LabRAM HR Evolution confocal Raman microscope. The excitation wavelength was 632.8 nm. A 100× objective with numerical aperture 0.90, a parallel analyzer configuration, and an 1800 lines/mm diffraction grating were used. For each incident polarization angle, Raman mapping acquired an array of 9 spectra with a 5 µm lateral step. The excitation power density was 125 kW/cm², the integration time was 10 s per point, and the laser spot area was 1.8 µm². Spectra for each polarization angle were averaged over the map, background-subtracted, and fit with Lorentzian lines. Polar plots of selected Raman peak intensities were generated from the fitted peak areas as a function of polarization angle.

experiment_description: Broadband optical characterization was performed on mechanically exfoliated bulk CdPS3 flakes on transparent substrates to retrieve the dielectric tensor over the ultraviolet, visible, near-infrared, and mid-infrared ranges. Polarization-resolved visible transmittance from 450 to 850 nm was measured on a CdPS3 flake exfoliated on Schott glass using a Zeiss Axio Lab.A1 optical microscope illuminated by a halogen source and coupled to an Optosky ATP5020P grating spectrometer through a Thorlabs M92L02 optical fiber with 200 µm core diameter; transmitted light was collected from a spot smaller than 15 µm using an N-Achroplan 50× Pol M27 objective with numerical aperture 0.8 while the incident polarization angle was varied. Normal-incidence reflectance and transmittance spectra were also acquired in the visible using a microscope/spectrometer configuration with an RX50M microscope and SOPTOP MPlanFL 50× objective with numerical aperture 0.8. Near- and mid-infrared spectra were measured using a Bruker Vertex 80v Fourier-transform infrared spectrometer coupled to a Hyperion 2000 infrared microscope with a 15× reflective objective of numerical aperture 0.4; the 900–1400 nm range used a tungsten-halogen lamp, CaF2 beamsplitter, and nitrogen-cooled MCT detector, while the 1400–17000 nm range used a Globar source and KBr beamsplitter. Spectroscopic ellipsometry was performed using an Accurion EP4 imaging ellipsometer in rotating-analyzer mode on two CdPS3 flakes of 50 nm and 165 nm thickness, over 250–1700 nm in 1 nm steps at incidence angles of 45°, 50°, 55°, and 60°. The dielectric response was extracted by global fitting of ellipsometry together with normal-incidence transmittance and reflectance spectra from multiple flakes over an overall spectral range of 250–16000 nm; the optical band edge was inferred from the retrieved absorption/extinction behavior, and the transparency-edge wavelength was defined using an extinction-coefficient threshold k = 0.01.

optical_bandgap_eV.description: Optical bandgap of CdPS3 inferred from broadband optical characterization and the absorption onset.

shortest_transparent_wavelength_for_k_0p.description: Shortest wavelength at which CdPS3 maintains high optical transparency under the paper's criterion that the extinction coefficient remains below k = 0.01.
